name: Production control
subject: One enclosed finished shirt side seam
action: Quality controller lifts fabric to check seam finish
environment: White inspection table, close oblique crop
prompt: One understated documentary photograph taken during real quality inspection in a premium fashion studio. Landscape 4:3. Close oblique view of the INSIDE of one fully finished dark navy cotton shirt, laid on a clean white inspection table. The only important feature is a real flat-felled side seam: two narrow parallel straight rows of ordinary small lockstitches, completely enclosed folded seam allowances, no raw edges or fraying. The seam runs diagonally through the center of the image. A single adult quality controller's normal thumb and index fingertip enter from bottom right and gently lift the nearby fabric to check that seam's strength and finish. Five-finger natural anatomy, restrained skin texture; only these fingertips need be visible. The shirt body continues naturally out of the frame. No buttons, buttonholes, collars, cuffs, embroidery, sketches, tools, labels, text, props, paper, drawn lines, dotted overlays or symbols. This must look like a normal honestly photographed seam, not exaggerated fibers, CGI or macro art. Soft neutral-white daylight, clean white table background, controlled simple composition. Finished garment only, no toile, basting or raw edges. One subject, one inspection action, no decorative staging.
